newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian cotton prices firm in limited trade.
newsitem.headline: Indian cotton prices firm in limited trade.

text.p: Cotton prices firmed on Monday in limited trade with dealers awaiting the outcome of political uncertinty in the country.
"Though prices are steady to firm, trading volumes are very low," said a leading cotton dealer.

In spot, Gujarat Kalyan gained 300 rupees to 13,500/13,800 rupees per candy (355.56 kg). Gujarat Shankar-4 (short-staple) recovered 500 rupees to 15,500/800 rupees per candy. Gujarat Wagad gained 300 rupees to 12,600 rupees per candy.
Punjab F-414 gained 10/50 rupees to 1,850/1,920 rupees per maund (37.32 kg).
Dealers said both farmers and traders were holding on to stocks awaiting the political situation to get back to normal.

On Monday, Inder Kumar Gujral, a leader of the United Front, a 13-party alliance, was sworn in as India's new prime minister after the defeat of the previous government of the same coalition on April 11 in a confidence vote.
"We are waiting for the formation of the new government and its policies," said another dealer.
